sections.heading: Dialogue

lines.en: What do you drink in the morning?

lines.ar: هَلْ تَذْهَبُ إِلَى الْمَكْتَبِ كُلَّ يَوْمٍ؟
lines.en: Do you go to the office every day?
No, sometimes I work at home.
And what do you do in the morning?
I read the news, then I write programs.

sections.note: Listen, then read it aloud. Play both roles. A colleague asks Ridhwan about his mornings.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.note: Present tense verbs take a prefix. Start with a for I, and ta for you, speaking to a man. Both end in u: aktubu, I write, and taktubu, you write.

sections.heading: Word builder: the root qaaf, raa, hamza, meaning reading

lines.en: a reader, the one who reads
read, the thing that is read

sections.note: You know faa-il, the doer, and maf-ool, the thing done to. Today's new pattern is fi-aala, the name of the activity itself. Qiraa-a means reading, as a habit or a hobby.

sections.heading: Speak it

lines.en: What do you drink in the morning?
Model answer: I drink tea in the morning.
Model answer: I'm working at the office today.
What do you write at work?
Model answer: I write programs for my company.

sections.note: Answer each question aloud about yourself. Then listen to the model answer.
